title: Skeleton shimmer
sub: Placeholder shimmers, then content fades in
html:
M
Maya R.Posted 2 min ago

Shipped the new onboarding flow today.
prompt: Build a skeleton loading state for a content card. Reproduce the real card's layout with placeholder blocks: an image block, an avatar square next to two short text lines, and one longer line, all filled with a pale grey-blue (#EFE7E0 style). Put one shimmer element over the whole skeleton: a 55% wide strip with linear-gradient(100deg, transparent, rgba(255,255,255,.85), transparent), animated with transform: translateX(-120%) to translateX(260%), 1.4s ease-in-out, infinite, inside a parent with overflow: hidden. Animating transform keeps it on the compositor, unlike animating background-position. When the data arrives, render the real content in the same grid cell as the skeleton and cross-fade (opacity .45s) so nothing shifts. Match placeholder sizes to the final content to avoid layout shift. Mark the loading region with aria-busy="true" and add a visually hidden role="status" message such as "Loading". Under prefers-reduced-motion replace the movement with a static state or a slow opacity fade. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Indeterminate bar
sub: A segment slides along a thin bar
html: Syncing workspacePlease wait
prompt: Build an indeterminate progress bar for a panel or page header. Make a 3px tall track (pale grey-blue, overflow: hidden, position: relative) that sits flush under the header. Inside it, a segment about 36% of the track width, filled with your accent gradient and rounded ends. Animate it with transform only: 0% translateX(-100%) scaleX(0.5), 50% translateX(130%) scaleX(1.3), 100% translateX(310%) scaleX(0.5), 1.6s, cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.25, 1), infinite, so the segment stretches as it speeds up and compresses at the ends like a material progress bar. Do not animate width or left. Use it for work with unknown duration; switch to a determinate bar (scaleX with transform-origin: left) as soon as you know the percentage. Dim and disable the content below while it runs. Mark the loading region with aria-busy="true" and add a visually hidden role="status" message such as "Loading". Under prefers-reduced-motion replace the movement with a static state or a slow opacity fade. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Dot bounce
html: Fetching results
prompt: Build a three-dot bounce loader. Three 16px circles filled with your accent gradient, 16px apart, each inside a 46px tall wrapper. Animate each dot with keyframes 0%, 60%, 100% translateY(0) and 30% translateY(-26px), 1.1s, cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0.3, 1), infinite, and delay the second and third dots by 0.15s and 0.3s so the bounce travels left to right. Add a small flat ellipse shadow under each dot that scales to 0.55 and fades to 0.5 opacity at the top of the bounce, in sync with the dot; this makes the motion read as a real bounce. Animate transform and opacity only. Add a short caption below ("Fetching results") in a muted color. Use it for short waits of unknown length, for example inside a button or an empty list state. Mark the loading region with aria-busy="true" and add a visually hidden role="status" message such as "Loading". Under prefers-reduced-motion replace the movement with a static state or a slow opacity fade. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Equalizer bars
sub: Bars rise and fall at their own rates
html:
Now playing2:41
Morning LightElena Voss
prompt: Build an equalizer loader for audio, uploads in progress or "now playing" states. Use 7-9 vertical bars, each 7px wide and a fixed height (about 62px) with rounded ends and a vertical blue gradient, aligned to the bottom in a flex row with 6px gaps. Set transform-origin: 50% 100% and animate transform: scaleY(0.18) to scaleY(1) with ease-in-out, infinite, alternate. Give every bar its own duration (0.7s to 1.4s) and a negative animation-delay so the bars are out of phase from the first frame and the pattern never visibly repeats. Animate transform only; never animate height. Put it inside a card with a small "Now playing" label and track title. For a stopped state set animation-play-state: paused and rest the bars at scaleY(0.2). Mark the loading region with aria-busy="true" and add a visually hidden role="status" message such as "Loading". Under prefers-reduced-motion replace the movement with a static state or a slow opacity fade. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Typing indicator
sub: Pulsing dots, then the message arrives
html:
Can we move our call to 3 PM?
Maya
Sure, 3 PM works. Sending a new invite now.
prompt: Build a chat typing indicator that hands over to the real message. In a conversation, render the sender's bubble with three 7px dots in a light blue, 5px apart, inside a bubble with a smaller bottom-left radius (16px 16px 16px 4px), a white background and a soft shadow. Pulse each dot with keyframes 0%, 70%, 100% opacity 0.3 scale(0.8) and 35% opacity 1 scale(1.15), 1.2s ease-in-out infinite, delaying dots by 0.16s and 0.32s. The typing bubble and the message bubble share one grid cell (grid-area: 1/1) so nothing jumps. Switch by toggling a data attribute: the typing bubble fades and scales out while the message springs in (transform from translateY(8px) scale(0.94), transform-origin at the bubble's tail, 590ms critically damped spring curve). Show the indicator only while a reply is genuinely pending, for at least about 600ms to avoid flicker. Mark the loading region with aria-busy="true" and add a visually hidden role="status" message such as "Loading". Under prefers-reduced-motion replace the movement with a static state or a slow opacity fade. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Logo draw
sub: A mark traces its stroke, then fills
html: Halo
prompt: Build a logo draw preloader with inline SVG. Add pathLength="1" to every path of the mark (an outline and an inner symbol), set stroke-dasharray: 1 and stroke-dashoffset: 1 so each path is invisible, then animate stroke-dashoffset from 1 to 0 so the line traces itself; stagger the inner symbol about 20% later than the outline. When the outline is complete, fade in a filled copy of the shape (opacity 0 to 1) and switch the inner symbol stroke to white so it reads on the fill, then fade in the wordmark with a small translateY(6px) rise. Total loop about 5s, ease-in-out, with the whole group fading out in the last 10% before it restarts. Use round caps and joins. For a real preloader, run the draw once, then remove the overlay when the page is ready; do not loop it forever. Mark the loading region with aria-busy="true" and add a visually hidden role="status" message such as "Loading". Under prefers-reduced-motion replace the movement with a static state or a slow opacity fade. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Percent preloader
sub: Count to 100, then the page slides in
html: 0%
prompt: Build a percentage preloader that reveals the page. Cover the viewport with a white overlay (position: fixed in production, absolute here) holding a big semibold percentage (60-80px, tabular-nums, tight tracking) with a small "%" and a 3px progress bar under it whose fill is a scaleX transform with transform-origin: left. Drive both from one requestAnimationFrame loop using an eased progress value so the count accelerates and settles; tie the value to real asset loading when you can, and clamp it so it never goes backwards. At 100, wait about 250ms, then slide the overlay up with transform: translateY(-100%) over 850ms using cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1), while the page content beneath rises from translateY(22px) and opacity 0 to its resting state. Remove the overlay from the DOM after the transition ends and restore scrolling. Show it only on first visit. Mark the loading region with aria-busy="true" and add a visually hidden role="status" message such as "Loading". Under prefers-reduced-motion replace the movement with a static state or a slow opacity fade. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Content pulse
html: Recent activity
prompt: Build a content pulse loading state, the calmer alternative to a shimmer. Render the real layout (for example a list of rows with a rounded thumbnail, two text lines and a small pill) using flat placeholder blocks in pale grey-blue. Animate each row's opacity from 0.4 to 1 and back with keyframes, 1.7s ease-in-out infinite, and stagger the rows with animation-delay of 0.25s each so the pulse travels down the list instead of the whole card blinking. Animate opacity only. Use the pulse when the list is short or the surface is small; use a shimmer for large image-heavy cards. Keep the placeholder geometry identical to the loaded rows to prevent layout shift, and swap in real content with a short opacity cross-fade. Mark the loading region with aria-busy="true" and add a visually hidden role="status" message such as "Loading". Under prefers-reduced-motion replace the movement with a static state or a slow opacity fade. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Blur-up image
sub: A blurry preview sharpens into the photo
html: Lake PlacidPreviewFull quality
prompt: Build a blur-up image loader. Render a tiny placeholder first (a 20-32px wide version of the photo, inlined as a data URI or a dominant-color gradient) scaled to fill the frame with filter: blur(9px) and transform: scale(1.15) so the blur edge is cropped by the container's overflow: hidden and border-radius. Stack the real image above it in the same container with opacity: 0 and filter: blur(12px), load it with the normal img element and decode() it, then when it is ready transition both to opacity: 1 and filter: blur(0) over about 600ms ease-out and remove the placeholder. Give the container a fixed aspect-ratio (or width and height attributes) so the page never shifts. Optionally show a small "Preview" chip that swaps to "Full quality". Do not animate the blur on large hero images, which is expensive; fade there instead. Mark the loading region with aria-busy="true" and add a visually hidden role="status" message such as "Loading". Under prefers-reduced-motion replace the movement with a static state or a slow opacity fade. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

prompt: Build a step checklist loader for a multi-stage task such as uploading, processing and finishing a file. Render the steps as a vertical list. Each step has a 20px circular marker, a bold label and a muted sub-line. States: pending (an empty ring in pale blue-grey), active (an accent ring with a small accent dot that pulses with scale 0.7 to 1.05, 1.1s ease-in-out infinite; not a rotating spinner) and done (a filled accent circle with a white check that pops in using a slight-overshoot spring). Draw a 2px vertical track behind the markers with an accent fill layer that grows with transform: scaleY(), transform-origin at the top, 700ms cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1). Drive the states from your real progress events, only ever moving forward, and put the current step in an aria-live="polite" region. Announce completion and errors in text, not just color. Mark the loading region with aria-busy="true" and add a visually hidden role="status" message such as "Loading". Under prefers-reduced-motion replace the movement with a static state or a slow opacity fade. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Morphing shape
sub: Square, circle and pill in a calm loop
prompt: Build a morphing shape loader. Use one 112px square element filled with your accent gradient inside a wrapper with filter: drop-shadow(0 10px 18px rgba(accent, .22)) (put the shadow on the wrapper, because box-shadow is clipped by clip-path). Animate its clip-path through three shapes: inset(0 round 24px) for a rounded square, inset(0 round 50%) for a circle, and inset(34px 0 round 999px) for a wide pill, then back to the square. Hold each shape for about 10-12% of the cycle with cubic-bezier(0.6, 0, 0.3, 1), 4.8s, infinite. clip-path animates without touching layout, and because the element never rotates it cannot be mistaken for a spinner. Add a small muted caption below. Keep the loop calm: nothing faster than about 2 seconds per shape change. Use it for splash screens or long background tasks. Mark the loading region with aria-busy="true" and add a visually hidden role="status" message such as "Loading". Under prefers-reduced-motion replace the movement with a static state or a slow opacity fade. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Liquid fill
sub: A rounded cup fills with wavy liquid
html: 0%
prompt: Build a liquid fill loader. Make a rounded container (92 by 128px, radius 28px, white, a 2px pale blue inset ring, overflow: hidden). Inside it put a liquid layer the full height of the container, positioned from the top, with a solid blue gradient body. Attach two wave strips to the top edge of the liquid: SVG paths 200% wide and 16px tall (a sine made from Q and T commands, one period per 100 units) in two blues, one lighter behind. Animate each strip with transform: translateX(0) to translateX(-50%), linear, infinite, at 2.6s and 3.8s in opposite directions so the waves interfere. Raise the level by setting the liquid layer's transform: translateY() from the full height to about -6px as progress goes 0 to 100, using real progress or an eased timer in requestAnimationFrame. Show the percentage beside the cup in a tabular-nums font. At 100, hold briefly, then drain or fade before resetting. Mark the loading region with aria-busy="true" and add a visually hidden role="status" message such as "Loading". Under prefers-reduced-motion replace the movement with a static state or a slow opacity fade. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.
